newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil, gasoline up sharply on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil, gasoline up sharply on Iraq.

text.p: Singapore oil products, with the exception of fuel oil, rose sharply on renewed tension between Iraq and the U.S. after Iraq fired a surface-to-air at two U.S. jets that were patrolling northern Iraq.

Gas oil (diesel) front month swaps rose to a record high of $28.25 on the back of fears the U.S. would launch a new missile attack on Iraq, traders said. October swaps closed 40 cents higher at $28.20/$28.30 than Wednesday.
The physical market rose sharply, with a bid by a major for 150,000 barrels at $28.08, about 50 cents above Wednesday's close, but the major failed to secure a seller.

Jet fuel firmed in line with the higher gas oil values despite talk of ample stocks in Singapore. Trade Development Board data showed middle distillate stocks rose to a 10-month high of 7.913 million barrels. Traders said more than 1 million was jet fuel.
Paper naphtha soared to record high levels with October talked 50 cents up at $21.15/$21.25 but the market was well supplied, traders said.
Gasoline initially resisted crude's gains until late in the trading day. Bids for 95-octane unleaded cargoes, lifting end September-early October, leapt to $22.90 from $21.60/$21.75.

"With naphtha so strong with crude and looking at the naphtha/mogas spread, the downside to mogas is limited," said a trader. But supplies were still ample with Singapore light distillate stocks rising 411,000 barrels to 5.645 million barrels, the TDB data showed.
Fuel oil was flat despite the news amid ample sellers. Residual stocks in Singapore rose more than 1 million barrels to 9.8 million barrel. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3093)
